events.text: The Great Fire of London begins in a bakery on Pudding Lane.
Britain uses the Julian calendar for the last time; the next day is 14 September.
The United States Department of the Treasury is founded.
The Carrington geomagnetic storm disrupts telegraph systems across Europe and North America.
Battle of Sedan: Emperor Napoleon III is captured by the Prussian army.
Japan formally surrenders aboard USS Missouri, ending the Second World War.
Ho Chi Minh proclaims the independence of Vietnam in Hanoi.
The first automated teller machine in the United States opens in Rockville Centre, New York.

births.text: Christa McAuliffe, American teacher and astronaut

deaths.text: J. R. R. Tolkien, English author of The Lord of the Rings
